newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Socialists want Italy in 1st euro wave - paper.
newsitem.headline: French Socialists want Italy in 1st euro wave - paper.

text.p: The French Socialist party, if it were elected, would refuse the exclusion of Italy from the first group of countries forming the euro and would conduct an audit of French public finances, a newspaper said on Friday.

Pierre Moscovici, a member of the Socialist Party leadership, told the La Tribune Desfosses newspaper that the Socialists would "engage in European discussions to judge the Maastricht criteria by trend."
He said "he refused the exclusion of Italy from the first group of countries participating in the single currency."
Moscovici said Wednesday's European Union forecasts for countries meeting the Maastricht GDP criteria were "optimistic for many countries, among which France."

For 1998, he said "we are on a trend for a public deficit of four percent of GDP," noting that in 1998 there will not be the benefits of one-off payments such as the France Telecom pension deal, which represents at 37.5 billion francs some 0.5 percent of GDP.
La Tribune said Moscivici believed the centre-right government had to prepare additional austerity measures to hit the three percent target.

"A Left-wing government will undertake a large audit of the French public finances and will start on that basis negotiations with our European Union partners to refine the economic convergence criterion in trends (rather than fixed figures)," Moscovici said.
He said this was "not re-negotiating the Maastricht Treaty" but would mean that "the decision to enter the euro will be taken on a political basis and not an accountancy basis."
"We envisage an economic government of the euro zone to coordinate the economic policies of the countries taking part in the single currency," Moscovici was quoted as saying in La Tribune.
